title: Perf Canary: Deploy/Release Annotations (runtime) — generation + propagation plan
content:
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Engineering)
Last edited: 2026-02-07
Status: in review (needs final sign-off from Telemetry + SRE)

Context
Perf-canary dashboards and regression alerts are only useful if we can reliably answer: “what changed?”

In practice, we need deploy/release metadata to show up in:
1) Grafana as vertical annotation markers on p95 latency + tokens/sec panels
2) Alert payload enrichment (“last deploy affecting this slice”, and link to diff)
3) Triage workflow (quickly correlate a regression with a runtime build rollout, region-by-region)

This doc defines:
- What constitutes a “deploy annotation event”
- Where it is generated (source of truth)
- How it is propagated into metrics/dashboards reliably
- Field schema, naming, and dedup rules
- Failure modes + operational checks

Non-goals
- Not defining the regression thresholds/baseline policy (see ADR-0231)
- Not standardizing all Redwood deploy events across all services (this is runtime + perf-canary scope)


1) Consumers + requirements

1.1 Dashboards (Grafana)
- Must render annotation markers for runtime changes at per-region granularity.
- Must support filtering by:
  - region
  - runtime_build / runtime_version
  - (nice-to-have) cluster / nodepool
- Must be available for at least 30d retention to support “last known good” comparisons.

1.2 Regression detector + alert enrichment
When a regression alert fires, payload needs:
- deploy marker time (closest prior marker; guard against out-of-order)
- runtime_build (git SHA + build ID) for the slice
- link(s): dashboard, deploy diff, and change list (PRs)

1.3 Paging hygiene
- Annotations must not be noisy (no per-pod restarts, no autoscaler churn markers)
- Emit only on “meaningful change” to runtime serving behavior:
  - runtime image rollout
  - runtime config change affecting kernels/scheduling
  - enabling/disabling “canary-safe” class behavior (only if it changes scheduling)


2) Definitions

2.1 What is a “deploy annotation event”
A deploy annotation event is a single, structured event emitted when a runtime rollout begins and when it is considered complete for a region (or cluster), containing enough metadata for correlation.

We standardize on two event types:
- runtime_deploy_start
- runtime_deploy_complete

Why both?
- Start is useful for suppressing alerts during rollout window.
- Complete is useful for post-deploy comparisons (and usually correlates better with stable perf).

We do NOT emit:
- pod restart events
- node replacements
- GPU driver patch markers (unless they are handled via a separate infra annotation stream)


3) Source of truth + generation

3.1 Primary source of truth: Release/Deploy controller
The deploy controller (release train / rollout tooling) is the authority for:
- what version is intended
- when a rollout was triggered
- per-region rollout plan and status

Therefore, the annotation event should be generated by the deploy controller, not inferred from runtime logs.

Rationale:
- avoids false markers from partial rollout
- avoids time skew and sampling artifacts
- supports “complete” semantics (controller knows when target is reached)

3.2 Secondary validation: runtime self-report (best-effort)
Runtime already propagates runtime_build + runtime_version through metrics/tracing for each request (see runtime PR 39180).
We use this to validate that a “complete” event matches what is actually serving.

If mismatch is detected (annotation says build X, but canary traffic reports build Y after 20 min), we file an auto ticket and flag the annotation stream as degraded.


4) Propagation path (end-to-end)

4.1 Event emission
Deploy controller emits events to telemetry ingestion as a small set of structured logs or OTEL events.

Minimum requirement:
- exactly-once is not required, but events must be idempotent with a stable event_id
- events must include a consistent timestamp basis (UTC)

4.2 Ingestion + storage
Telemetry/Observability pipeline stores these events in the “deploy-annotations” metrics namespace (implementation detail: Grafana annotation datasource backed by the same stack we use for other deploy markers).

Key properties:
- low cardinality
- retention >= 30d (prefer 90d)
- queryable by tags (service, region, env)

4.3 Dashboard consumption
Grafana dashboards use the annotation datasource to overlay markers.

Panel rules:
- Show only runtime_deploy_complete by default.
- Provide a toggle to show deploy_start (useful during incident triage).

4.4 Alerting consumption
Perf-canary regression detector looks up “most recent runtime_deploy_complete” for the slice’s region + env.
The detector includes in the alert payload:
- deploy event timestamp
- runtime_build, runtime_version
- rollout_id
- link: Grafana panel with time range anchored to deploy time


5) Field schema (v1)

We keep schema minimal and stable. Labels/fields are tuned for low cardinality; anything high-cardinality belongs in logs, not metrics.

Required fields
- event_id: stable unique id for dedup (recommend: rollout_id + region + event_type)
- event_type: runtime_deploy_start | runtime_deploy_complete
- service: always “serving-runtime” (string)
- environment: prod | staging
- region: us-east | eu-west | …
- rollout_id: release train identifier (string)
- runtime_version: human-friendly (e.g., “runtime-2026.02.05”) — if we have it
- runtime_build_id: canonical build identifier (string; may include date/build number)
- git_sha: full or short SHA (standardize on 12-char short_sha in dashboards, full in logs)
- initiated_by: “release-train” or username/service principal
- timestamp_utc: RFC3339

Optional fields (include if available without adding cardinality pain)
- change_summary: short text (<= 120 chars) for Grafana tooltip; example “Rollout runtime-2026.02.05 (kernel autotune patch)”
- config_fingerprint: hash of runtime config bundle (helps correlate non-image changes)
- artifact_uri: link to image digest / build artifact
- pr_list: comma-separated PR ids (ONLY if already computed; do not compute dynamically in pipeline)

Explicitly NOT included in the annotation event (v1)
- gpu_sku (slice attribute; should be handled by request metrics + dashboard filters)
- scheduler_mode (request-level tag; changes frequently and can cause noisy markers)
- model (too many; also rollouts are runtime-wide)


6) Naming conventions

6.1 Service name
- Use “serving-runtime” consistently across annotation stream and request metrics tags.
- Avoid variants: “runtime”, “inference-runtime”, etc.

6.2 Region naming
- Must match the label used by perf-canary metrics (e.g., region=us-east, region=eu-west)
- If cloud provider region differs (us-east-1), map to Redwood region at emission time.

6.3 Versioning
- runtime_version is a release-train-friendly string.
- runtime_build_id is the canonical build id used by runtime metrics tag runtime_build.
- If only one is available, emit that one and keep the other blank (but do not invent).


7) Dedup + ordering rules

7.1 Dedup (ingestion)
Events are considered duplicates if event_id matches.
- Keep the earliest timestamp_utc seen for that event_id.
- Store a “duplicate_count” internal metric for health monitoring.

7.2 Ordering (consumer)
Consumers should not assume events arrive ordered.
Dashboard annotation queries should order by timestamp_utc.
Regression detector should:
- query for the latest runtime_deploy_complete event strictly <= regression window end
- ignore events that occur after the metric datapoint timestamp


8) Rollout windows + alert suppression hooks

We want to reduce false positives during rollouts.

Policy (align with ADR-0231 and SRE guidance):
- If runtime_deploy_start exists in the last X minutes AND runtime_deploy_complete not yet observed, regression alerts switch to “ticket-only” or suppressed for that region.
- After runtime_deploy_complete, apply a warmup grace period (default 15 minutes) before paging.

Notes:
- The warmup grace is separate from canary workload warmup; this is specifically “fleet is stabilizing after rollout.”


9) Health checks / operational readiness

9.1 Daily automated check (recommended)
For each region in prod:
- verify at least one runtime_deploy_complete event exists in last 14d
- verify that runtime_build from canary request metrics matches the latest deploy_complete’s runtime_build_id within 30 minutes of deploy completion
- verify annotation query latency (Grafana datasource query < 2s)

9.2 Manual triage checklist when annotations look wrong
- Are we missing all annotations (pipeline outage) or just one region?
- Did a rollback happen? (look for two deploy_complete events in short interval)
- Does canary traffic show a different runtime_build than annotation claims?
- Is region mapping misconfigured? (us-east vs us-east-1)

Escalation:
- Missing events: Telemetry oncall
- Mismatch with actual runtime_build: Release Engineering + Runtime


10) Examples

10.1 Example deploy_complete event (human view)
2026-02-05T19:42:10Z  runtime_deploy_complete
service=serving-runtime  env=prod  region=eu-west
rollout_id=rt-2026-02-05.3
runtime_version=runtime-2026.02.05
runtime_build_id=rb-90217
git_sha=8c1f2a6d91e3
change_summary=Rollout runtime-2026.02.05 (scheduler pinning defaults)

10.2 Example event_id
rt-2026-02-05.3:eu-west:runtime_deploy_complete

10.3 Grafana annotation tooltip (expected)
serving-runtime deploy complete
region: eu-west
runtime: runtime-2026.02.05 (rb-90217)
sha: 8c1f2a6d91e3
rollout: rt-2026-02-05.3


11) Known issues / open questions

- Q: Should infra-driven events (GPU driver rollout, node image) be part of this same stream?
  Proposal: no, keep separate “infra-annotations” stream; dashboards may show both with toggles.

- Q: How do we annotate partial rollouts (e.g., 30% canary within region)?
  Proposal (v1): treat runtime_deploy_start as “partial begins” and runtime_deploy_complete as “100% reached”. If we need % markers later, add optional field rollout_phase.

- Q: What’s the canonical place to compute “PR list included in release”? 
  Proposal: release train can attach a short summary + link to release notes; do not inline large PR lists into annotations.

- Q: Time source: controller clock vs CI timestamp?
  Proposal: use controller emission time (UTC). CI build time is informative but not what dashboards need.


12) Implementation pointers (what changed where)

- Runtime emits request tags: runtime_build, runtime_version, scheduler_mode (request-scoped) and supports deploy annotations hook (see runtime PR 39180).
- Observability pack adds Grafana dashboard JSON and annotation datasource usage (see PR 844).
- Alert rules and regression semantics incorporate maintenance/rollout suppression (see PR 851 and slo-toolkit PR 410).


13) Action items

Release Engineering (Connor)
- [ ] Confirm rollout_id format and event_id convention with SRE + Telemetry
- [ ] Add release-train task: emit runtime_deploy_start/complete per region

Telemetry (Logan / Caleb)
- [ ] Confirm ingestion path for annotation events + retention
- [ ] Validate cardinality + tags allowed (service/env/region/event_type)

SRE (Sean / Rafael)
- [ ] Confirm suppression policy defaults (grace period duration, paging behavior)

Dashboards (Felix)
- [ ] Ensure panels display only deploy_complete by default + filter controls

Perf-canary (Noah / Marcus)
- [ ] Alert payload: include latest deploy_complete details + time-anchored dashboard links
